messages:
alex: customer reports 400 from /v1/rerank even though payload validates locally. sending repro below — can someone confirm server parsing error?

alex: curl they used (notice the leading bytes):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\    -d $'\\uFEFF[{"id":"1","query":"what is x","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"x"}]}]'
```

alex: server response: 400 Invalid JSON payload

alex: raw log snippet from our gateway: 
```
parse_error: invalid character '\\u00ef' at start of value
path: /v1/rerank
client: cust-8472
```

maria: :eyes: looks like a UTF-8 BOM (\\uFEFF) prefixed to the body. some Windows editors / older clients include it. our JSON parser chokes on the 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF sequence.

sam: we saw a similar flake with a Node SDK that did not strip BOM on stringified payloads. which client do they use?

alex: customer says their integration is Ruby on Windows, sending body from an external service that may wrap the payload. they attached a file that begins with EF BB BF.

maria: quick workaround: advise customer to remove BOM before POSTing, or set Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and ensure the client encodes without BOM. also can do server-side trim on first char if it's \\uFEFF.

maria: longer fix: add a small pre-parse sanitizer that discards leading \\uFEFF bytes before decoding. low risk, low perf cost.

sam: filing a bug against our SDKs to ensure .stringify() flows never emit BOM. will also add a note in our troubleshooting KB.

jenny: customer wants a plain step they can run now — can we give a one-liner they can try to confirm?

maria: yep. for their Ruby example:
```ruby
body = File.read('payload.json', mode: 'rb').sub(/^\\uFEFF/, '')
HTTP.headers('Content-Type' => 'application/json').post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank', :body => body)
```

maria: or a curl test that strips the BOM on Linux: `tail -c +4 file_with_bom.json | curl -X POST ... --data @-`

alex: I sent the workaround to the customer and asked for the raw file. they confirmed the file started with the 3 BOM bytes. they applied the Ruby change and call succeeded (200).

sam: I'll open an RFC to add a tiny sanitizer in the request pipeline for rerank+ranking endpoints. will include a feature-flag roll out.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout of request-sanitizer v0.1 to staging at 2024-11-06T15:30:00Z

jenny: thanks team — please add KB article and paste it into the support ticket. customer flagged as P2 since it blocks ingestion.

maria: KB slug suggestion: '400-on-rerank-due-to-utf8-bom' with steps: detection, quick client workarounds, server mitigation status.

alex: resolved for customer (they confirmed after workaround). leaving this thread open until sanitizer RFC + KB PR are merged. :white_check_mark:
